_comment: Short world events. trigger: day_start | enter:<location_id>. Conditions: weekdays, blocks, min_day, max_day, job, no_job, min_rep, min_sets, flag, not_flag, housing, min_cash, max_cash. once: fires at most once. chance rolled on the world RNG stream.

events.text: Your phone buzzes. It's Dad. 'So is this comedy thing a job, or a phase?'

choices.text: Say it's going great. (It is not.)

events.text: There's a crumpled twenty in the pocket of your other jeans.
Heat advisory. Even the pigeons are walking in the shade.
Mari taps the rent calendar. 'Week's almost up. I'm not a bank, but I'm also not a monster.'
The top-bunk guy is watering his plant at midnight and humming. He waves. He has a mail slot.

choices.text: Ask how long he's lived here.

events.text: Deshawn is in the bucket line, rehearsing his minute under his breath. 'Twentieth time,' he says. 'Feels lucky.'
A regular at the bar keeps yelling 'Do the one about airplanes!' at every comic.

choices.text: Watch how the host handles him.
Buy him a drink to shut him up.

events.text: A tourist on a scooter takes out a trash can and three pigeons. Nobody is hurt. The pigeons are furious.
Priya slides you a napkin: 'Guy at table four is writing a screenplay called AUSTIN. Just Austin.'

choices.text: Tell her she should do standup.

events.text: Lonnie Szabo is at the bar after his set. 'You're the kid from the open mic. Short setups. Get to the funny.'

choices.text: Thank him and leave him alone.

events.text: Bea Calloway, the Lantern Room booker, is in the back of the Spur with a notebook.

choices.text: Let your set do the talking.

events.text: A surge alert pings: double pay for the next hour.
You can't find your wallet. It turns up in the hostel fridge, minus fifteen dollars and plus a note: 'sorry'.
Mari leaves a plate of leftover tamales on your bunk with a sticky note: 'Eat. Then go earn rent.'
The night clerk tells you he's seen four comics quit this month. 'You've got the look of a fifth.'
It's Monday. The line for the Mothership is already forming around the block.
Rhonda texts: 'Short-staffed tonight. If you can pick up the door, I'll remember it.'
Dusty waves you over. 'Got a guy who flaked. Want to go up early? Real crowd still here.'
Sudden downpour. Sixth-floor gutters empty onto the sidewalk like a waterfall.

choices.text: Wait it out under an awning.

events.text: You dreamed your name got pulled and you forgot every word. You woke up mouthing your minute.
